title: Treasury cash-management buyback operation (1Mo-2Y nominal, $12.5B cap, 1:40pm ET) — the largest single operation on the August-refunding schedule
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35 — byte-identical to the 2026-09-05 fetch, so sb0607's promised replacement schedule is still unpublished 20 days on). Text layer independently decompressed and the row re-read verbatim: announce 9/8/2026, operation 9/9/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/10/2026, Cash Management, Nominal Coupons 1Mo to 2Y, maturity range 10/10/2026 - 09/09/2028, min $0, max $12.5 billion. STAYS ESTIMATE for one measured reason rather than an inherited one: the confirming primary is the operation announcement, which treasurydirect.gov publishes at 11:00am ET on the announcement date, and this research ran at 10:10am ET on 2026-09-08 — the announcement did not exist yet. The 09-03 sibling operation's announcement (BBPA_20260903174000.xml, HTTP 200, fetched this session) is the template it will follow. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by this event's own never-assessed initial research on 2026-09-08, standing in for proposals/treasury-buyback-cash-mgmt-2026-09-09.from-treasury-20y-bond-2026-09-15.json (the only proposal for this id), which is now shadowed and stays where it is. WHAT THE RESEARCH CHANGED FROM THE PROPOSAL, both stated because a canonical file should not silently inherit a claim it disproved. (1) IMPACT RAISED low -> medium. Every other buyback operation this calendar tracks is medium (treasury-buyback-10y20y-*, treasury-buyback-20y30y-*, treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06, treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09), and this one is 6.25x the size of any of them; filing the biggest operation on the schedule below the $2B ones was the inconsistency, not the tier. (2) THE PROPOSAL'S SIZE CLAIM IS OVERSTATED AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It reads 'larger than every long-end operation on the whole August-refunding schedule combined'; re-reading the same PDF row by row, the schedule carries nine long-end nominal operations (five 10Y-20Y, four 20Y-30Y) at $2B each = $18B, against this operation's $12.5B. The defensible version: $12.5B is 6.25x ANY SINGLE long-end operation (3.1x after sb0607's doubling), and the two September cash-management operations together ($25B) do exceed the long end's $18B — but one operation alone does not. WHAT SURVIVED AND IS NOW MEASURED: cash-management buybacks are a SEPARATE PROGRAMME from liquidity support, not a big version of one. All 26 on record (api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations, 219 rows, fetched 2026-09-08) are 1Mo-2Y; they run in clusters around quarter-turns; they take the full cap 22 of 26 times and >=96% of it 24 of 26; and offers have exceeded the cap in every single one (min cover 1.43x), so a short fill is Treasury refusing prices, never running out of paper. TWO CAUTIONS INHERITED FROM THE PROPOSAL, both still true. The sector is 1Mo-2Y: it buys nothing at any tenor the long-end ledgers care about, so this is a cash/front-end supply signal, not duration support. And $12.5B is a ceiling, not a forecast. symbols: [], no house playbook is macro-keyed, and nothing here licenses an entry.
